structured.rankingRationale: Rail Day, CILA and Electricity Transformation Canada rank highest because their published audiences are directly tied to transit/infrastructure/energy and their multi-day or programme formats fit a 157-room downtown hotel without claiming a room block. Land & Development follows for its published senior development audience and MTCC proximity. BSO is geographically strong but one day and outside the core infrastructure focus. CIGRE is strategically relevant but ranks lower because the current edition is committed to Westin Harbour Castle.

notesForDeepResearch: Prioritize Rail Day, CILA and Electricity Transformation Canada for infrastructure-fit validation; verify any separate hotel, speaker or exhibitor housing channel.
Treat Land & Development as executive side-meeting/overflow opportunity rather than assumed citywide room demand.
For CIGRE, pursue future-edition relationship development or documented overflow/adjacent meeting needs only.
materialUncertainties: No candidate has a published room block or peak-room figure in the reviewed evidence.
Absence of a hotel partner was treated as unconfirmed, not open sourcing.
The candidate set is infrastructure/construction/energy and adjacent screen-industry demand; no evidenced incentive-recognition programme met the Toronto and date/venue constraints.
CIGRE current-edition venue is a named competing hotel and is not treated as open inventory.

result.text: Six future Toronto event-driven opportunities were identified within the supplied date and territory constraints, with venue commitments, sourcing uncertainty, hotel fit, and competitive constraints stated explicitly. Four additional candidates were flagged or rejected because of territory, scale, or missing exact venue evidence.
